Maladaptive Strategies.value: I throw myself into work or tasks to keep my mind occupied
go over and over why the event happened to me
I dwell on how I used to be before the event

Memory.value: My memories of the frightening event are very clear and detailed.
Remembering what happened during the frightening event is just like looking at photographs of it in my mind.
When I remember the frightening event I feel like it is happening right now.

vignette: Margaret had been a ship captain for over forty years. Known for her sharp mind and unwavering resolve, she was accustomed to handling complex situations with ease. However, nothing could have prepared her for the nightmarish encounter with police violence that forever altered her life. On a stormy evening in 2018, Margaret found herself at the center of a violent confrontation with law enforcement. She had been docked at a port and was questioned about an unrelated incident. The exchange quickly escalated into an altercation where she was viciously assaulted by several officers, leaving her shaken and traumatized. Since that fateful night, Margaret's memories have remained vivid and hauntingly clear. Every detail of the violent encounter feels as if it were imprinted in her mind like a photograph. When she closes her eyes, she is transported back to that moment; the sounds, smells, and sights are all too real. She relives the event, feeling the fear and helplessness wash over her once again. Margaret has found herself grappling with these memories almost constantly. To cope, she throws herself into work, often working long hours on the ship to keep her mind occupied. The more she tries to distract herself through intense focus on tasks, the more vividly the memories return. Her rumination on why this happened to her and dwelling on how different things used to be before the event only exacerbates the intrusive thoughts. She spends countless nights going over every detail of that night, wondering what could have been done differently to prevent the violence. The clarity of these memories haunts her, making it nearly impossible for her to relax or let go of the trauma. Margaret had come to believe that if she worked harder and longer, she could distract herself from these painful recollections. However, this strategy has not helped as much as she hoped. Instead, the more she immerses herself in work to avoid thinking about the event, the stronger her memories become. The images are so clear that they feel like they are happening again right now. Her vivid recall of the assault is relentless and overwhelming, making it difficult for Margaret to find any respite. Her days have become a cycle of intense work followed by intrusive thoughts and reliving the traumatic event at night. This pattern has taken a toll on her physical health as well; she frequently experiences insomnia and exhaustion from both overworking and the sheer mental strain of repressing these memories. Margaret's closest friend, who is also a fellow captain, noticed that something was off in recent months. She commented on Margaret’s increased hours at work and how she seemed distant and more agitated than usual. Her family, especially her grown children, have expressed concern about her well-being but struggle to understand the depth of her distress. The relentless nature of these memories, combined with her maladaptive coping mechanisms, has made it increasingly difficult for Margaret to maintain her once vibrant life. She knows that something must change; she is afraid that this cycle will continue to worsen and impact her ability to function effectively as a captain. What finally brought her to seek help was the realization that no matter how hard she tried to push away these memories, they continued to haunt her. Margaret hopes that with professional guidance, she can find healthier ways to cope and perhaps start to heal from this traumatic experience. Her greatest fear is being forever trapped in that nightmarish memory, but her deepest hope lies in reclaiming a sense of peace and control over her life once again.
